title: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii Nuclear Transformation by Electroporation
author: João itor Molino
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bx5cpq2w
materials: Aseptically inoculate 250 mL, Tap media with wild type cells. Either by scrappeing cells of a plate with a inocculating loop or from a previous cultured cells. Incubate at 25 °C , under constant shaking (~150-180 RPM) and light (60-80 µmols de photons/m 2 s) until a cell density from 3 x 10^6 cells/mL to 6 x 10^6 cells/mL is reached. Pellet cells in centrifuge tubes. Separate culture in sufficient amount of sterile 50mL centrifuge tubes or larger volume tubes, and centrifuge for 2000 x g, 25 °C, 10 minutes . Pellet Cells Genttly ressupend cells at 3-6-10 8 cells/mL in Transformation Buffer. MAX Efficiency™ Transformation Reagent for Algae Thermo Fisher Catalog #A24229 Culture at 3x10 6 cells/mL usually yield 12-13 transformations.

steps.title: Digest and purify plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: Set up a restriction digest of 40 µg uncut vector using appropriate flanking enzymes to linearize the expression cassette; incubate the reaction for 6 h at 37 °C; purify the digested DNA with a PCR‑purification kit (avoid gel purification); quantify the purified DNA by absorbance (e.g., Nanodrop) aiming for a concentration of 250–700 ng/µL (example result 0.641 µg/µL, 30 µL eluted, total 19.230 µg).

steps.title: Mix DNA with cells in cuvette
steps.instruction: Add 250–1000 ng of the linearized vector to the bottom of an electroporation cuvette; add 250 µL of Chlamydomonas cells resuspended at ~3 × 10⁸ cells/mL; pipette up and down, flick, and shake the cuvette to bring cells to the bottom; include a no‑DNA control cuvette containing elution buffer or water; incubate the mixtures on ice for 10 min.

steps.title: Electroporate and short recovery
steps.instruction: Wipe the cuvette exterior to remove condensed water; electroporate using the settings listed in the “Table Electroporation” (Gene Pulser Xcell, Biorad, 1652660); after the pulse, let the cuvette sit for a further 10 min to allow cells to recover.

steps.title: Overnight recovery in TAP/sucrose
steps.instruction: Transfer the electroporated cells to a sterile 50 mL centrifuge tube containing 10 mL TAP medium with 40 mM sucrose, pH 7.0; rinse the cuvette with additional TAP/40 mM sucrose to collect any remaining cells; incubate the tube at room temperature on a rocker or shaker set to 50 rpm overnight under ambient light.

steps.title: Plate cells on selective media
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the overnight culture at 2000 × g, 25 °C for 10 min; aseptically discard the supernatant; resuspend the pellet in 300 µL TAP/40 mM sucrose; dispense 200 µL onto each of two agar plates containing the appropriate antibiotic; let the droplets dry aseptically without a lid, then spread cells evenly with an inoculation loop while avoiding plate edges; seal plates with parafilm and incubate under constant light (60 µmol photons·m⁻²·s⁻¹) at 25 °C; colonies should appear in 5–7 days.
